author: reek
body: Which medium is mine? On a real machine several controllers carry disks at once -- the internal SATA drive on AHCI, the boot stick on USB -- and GopDisk's dispatch order would hand every read to the internal drive, whose GPT is not ours, whose ESP holds someone else's loader, and whose contents no ceremony should touch. The boot medium is identified by CONTENT, not by which controller answers first: it is the disk whose EFI System Partition carries our own CODEX.CDX.

author: reek
body: The probe rides the very seam it configures. GopDisk's selection cells steer disk-read-sector; setting them to a candidate makes the whole FAT stack above (GPT walk, ESP mount, root-directory lookup) read from that candidate, so one gfat-file-size call answers the question. A hit leaves the cells locked and every later read -- storage screens, wake ceremony, identity save -- lands on the proven medium. No hit anywhere clears the cells, and the dispatch order stands as before, which on a single-disk machine was already right.

author: reek
body: USB is probed first: when a stick carrying CODEX.CDX is present it is almost certainly what the machine booted from, and probing it first keeps a development machine's internal Codex install from shadowing the stick in hand. The USB candidate exists only when usb-attach published a disk handle -- probing through the connect fallback would reset the shared controller and kill the keyboard.

author: reek
body: The NVMe candidate connects (and publishes its handle) on first touch; a machine without the controller answers the PCI scan with nothing and the probe costs one walk of the bus.

author: reek
body: Returns the selected kind, zero when no medium carries CODEX.CDX -- in which case the cells are cleared and GopDisk's dispatch order decides, exactly as before this chapter existed.
